issue: Is restitution under the Mandatory Victim Restitution Act a criminal punishment for purposes of the Ex Post Facto Clause?
provision: U.S. Const. art. I, § 9, cl. 3 (Ex Post Facto Clause); 18 U.S.C. § 3663A (MVRA)

sides.position: MVRA restitution is not a criminal punishment for Ex Post Facto purposes (as the opinion's description of the split implies; the excerpts do not state this holding expressly)
cases: United States v. Ellingburg, 113 F.4th 839 (8th Cir. 2024)

sides.position: MVRA restitution is a criminal penalty carrying characteristics of criminal punishment, so it cannot be applied retroactively in violation of the Ex Post Facto Clause
cases: United States v. Siegel, 153 F.3d 1256 (11th Cir. 1998)
United States v. Kluge, No. 23-10697 (11th Cir. 2025)

quote: to address a circuit split on whether restitution under the Mandatory Victim Restitution Act is a criminal punishment for purposes of the Ex Post Facto Clause.
cite: United States v. Karl Patrick Kluge, No. 23-10697 (11th Cir. 2025)
